title: Coding Set 02: Number Theory & Array Equalization
description: Reported HCL coding rounds: prime check / smallest prime factor and equalizing array elements via step X.

problems.title: Prime or Smallest Prime Divisor
problems.statement: Given an integer N (N >= 2), determine if N is prime. If N is prime, print 'PRIME'. Otherwise, print its smallest prime divisor (> 1).
problems.outputFormat: Print 'PRIME' if N is prime, else print the smallest prime divisor.

problems.timeComplexity: O(sqrt(N)) trial division using odd divisors after 2.
edgeCases: Large prime up to 10^9+7 requires `long` (`d * d <= n` avoids overflow up to 10^12)

problems.title: Array Equalization by Adding or Subtracting X
problems.statement: You are given an integer array A of size N and a positive integer X. In one operation, you may add X to or subtract X from any single element of A. Determine whether all elements of A can be made equal. If impossible, print -1; otherwise print the minimum total number of operations required.
problems.inputFormat:
Line 1: Two integers N and X.
Line 2: N space-separated integers A[0..N-1].
problems.outputFormat: A single integer: minimum operations or -1.

solutions.python:
import sys

data = list(map(int, sys.stdin.read().split()))
n, x = data[0], data[1]
a = data[2:2+n]
rem = a[0] % x
if any(v % x != rem for v in a):
    print(-1)
else:
    a.sort()
    med = a[n // 2]
    print(sum(abs(v - med) // x for v in a))

problems.timeComplexity: O(N log N) due to sorting to find the median.
problems.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra space beyond input array.
edgeCases: Negative numbers require Euclidean non-negative modulo `((a[i] % x) + x) % x` in Java
Median minimizes sum of L1 distances `|a[i] - target|`
Sum of operations can exceed 32-bit `int`, so use `long`
